name: Upper Grand Valley Dani
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Bromley, H. Myron 1961. The phonology of Lower Grand Valley Dani (Verhandelingen KITLV 34) - compares Grand Valley dialects incl. Upper Grand Valley

sources.citation: Bromley, H. Myron. 1981. A Grammar of Lower Grand Valley Dani. Pacific Linguistics C-63. Canberra: ANU. xiv+424 pp.
sources.note: Lower Grand Valley only. Orthography note (printed p. 67, ch. 3 n. 1 and n. 3): hyphen marks 'a juncture separating a preceding fully-stressed form from a post-cliticised form with no stress or suppressed stress'; 'Clitics are in Dani postposed units which are stressless or have suppressed stress... (compare Bromley 1961:49-52)'. Nothing on the upper-valley dialects beyond one lexical footnote ('mid and upper valley term bpakel forest animal').

sources.citation: transnewguinea.org / Lexibank, 'Dani, Upper Grand Valley' (wordlist from Bromley 1967)
sources.note: Wordlist only (Bromley 1967 forms, occasional phonetic bracketing); nothing on stress.

sources.citation: van der Stap, P. A. M. 1966. Outline of Dani Morphology. Verhandelingen KITLV 48. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff. viii+195 pp.
sources.note: Describes Mugogo Dani 'around the Government Post Wamena' (Preface p. V), 'in between Bromley's Lower Aikhe Dani and his Lower Grand Valley Dani' (p. 2). 'After the expert description of Dani Phonology by Myron Bromley, there is no need for a further description' (p. 2); phoneme chart pp. 3-4. Zero occurrences of stress/accent in either scanned layer. Silent on stress; not uppe1430.

sources.citation: Bromley, H. Myron. 1961. The Phonology of Lower Grand Valley Dani: A Comparative Structural Study of Skewed Phonemic Patterns. Verhandelingen KITLV 34. 's-Gravenhage: Nijhoff. xvi+98 pp. (ch. II 'Survey of phonemic patterns of Dani dialects', pp. 6-19 = Glottolog ref 602157 for uppe1430)
sources.note: For the upper-valley dialects (sec. 2.3 Wodo Dani pp. 10-11, sec. 2.4 Lower Kibin Dani p. 11) only consonant/vowel inventories and phoneme distribution; 'stress' first appears in ch. III (p. 21), which describes Lower Grand Valley Dani only: sec. 3.132 p. 49 'The phonological word consists of a syllable or group of syllables with only one primary word stress. Since this stress occurs on final syllables of words in most cases...'; unpredictable 'independent secondary stress' pp. 50-52; clitics stressless (p. 52). No stress statement for Upper Grand Valley Dani.
